definition: Clinical efficacy is how well a clinical intervention works in improving symptoms or related outcomes in the people or disorders it is intended to help. In this context, it refers to judging whether Guided Imagery and Music has beneficial effects across mood disorder groups and symptom areas.

reasons: The definition’s core wording (“how well a clinical intervention works in improving symptoms or related outcomes”) is a generic conception of efficacy that is not explicitly supported by the provided packet text.

The packet mentions that the review will “Evaluate clinical efficacy and transdiagnostic potential across diverse mood disorder populations and symptom domains,” but it does not substantiate the specific framing in the definition as the requested meaning of the term itself.

The definition ties “clinical efficacy” specifically to “Guided Imagery and Music” and “beneficial effects across mood disorder groups and symptom areas,” while the packet only states the aim to evaluate clinical efficacy (not that such beneficial effects have been established or that “clinical efficacy” is defined in these terms).
The first sentence gives a broad, generic definition of clinical efficacy that is not stated in the packet and goes beyond the supplied source.
